title: Countable coordinate support of a countably generated linear image
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $L$ an $R$-module generated by an at most countable subset (every element is a finite $R$-linear combination of its elements), $J$ a set, and $(N_j)_{j\in J}$ any family of $R$-modules. Put $M=\bigoplus_{j\in J}N_j$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules], and let $h:L\to M$ be $R$-linear. For $v\in M$ let $\operatorname{supp}(v)=\{j\in J:v_j\ne0\}$. There exists a sequence $(g_n)_{n\in\mathbf N}$ generating $L$ such that, for $F=\bigcup_{n\in\mathbf N}\operatorname{supp}(h(g_n))$, the set $F$ is at most countable and $\operatorname{supp}(h(x))\subseteq F$ for every $x\in L$. Equivalently $h(L)\subseteq M_F$, where $M_F$ is the coordinate submodule of [def-trf-coordinate-submodule]. No countability of $R$ or of the underlying sets of $L$ and the $N_j$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 058X, theorem-kaplansky-direct-sum, proof lines 20511-20536: choose countable generators and collect finite coordinate supports of their images under the P- and Q-projections; stated for an arbitrary linear map from a countably generated module.

proof.text: Choose a generating subset $G\subseteq L$ and an injection $a:G\hookrightarrow\mathbf N$, which exist by the at most countable generation hypothesis. Set $g_n$ equal to the unique $g\in G$ with $a(g)=n$ when one exists, and to $0$ otherwise. Each member of $G$ occurs, so this sequence generates $L$. This construction includes $G=\varnothing$: then $L=0$ and every $g_n=0$.

source.place: Tag 058X, theorem-kaplansky-direct-sum, proof lines 20511–20536: countable generators and finite coordinate supports of their projected images.

proof.text: Put $S_n=\operatorname{supp}(h(g_n))$ and $F=\bigcup_n S_n$. Each $S_n$ is finite by [def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules]. Choose for each $n$ an injection $b_n:S_n\hookrightarrow\mathbf N$. For $j\in F$ let $n(j)$ be the least $n$ with $j\in S_n$. The map $j\mapsto(n(j),b_{n(j)}(j))$ is injective into $\mathbf N^2$, and composing with $(u,v)\mapsto (u+v)(u+v+1)/2+v$ gives an injection into $\mathbf N$ (successive values of $u+v$ give disjoint consecutive intervals). Hence $F$ is at most countable, including when all $S_n$ are empty.

source.place: Tag 058X, theorem-kaplansky-direct-sum, proof lines 20511–20536: countable generators and finite coordinate supports of their projected images.

proof.text: For $x\in L$ choose a finite expression $x=\sum_{k=1}^t r_k g_{n_k}$. If $j\notin F$, then $h(g_{n_k})_j=0$ for every $k$ by the definition of $F$. Linearity of $h$ and the componentwise operations of [def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules] give $h(x)_j=\sum_{k=1}^t r_k h(g_{n_k})_j=0$. Thus $\operatorname{supp}(h(x))\subseteq F$. By [def-trf-coordinate-submodule] this says exactly $h(x)\in M_F$, proving the asserted image inclusion. The same calculation handles the empty sum. Only the index set of generators and finite supports were counted, never elements of $R$, $L$, or $N_j$.
